scientific_question: Among fully species-disjoint Lepidoptera, does overlap in native larval host-resource geography predict congruent post-IBD spatial genetic structure beyond insect sampling geometry and simple resource-breadth similarity?

single_successor_change.definition: mean of Laplacian similarities in panel-standardized log1p resolved native host-species count and log1p native WGSRPD3 footprint-unit count
single_successor_change.purpose: distinguish which host-resource regions overlap from merely having similarly broad host-resource repertoires

primary_predictor.raw: Jaccard similarity of frozen native WCVP-v13 WGSRPD3 host-resource footprint sets

pairwise_transfer_surface.pair_transfer_congruence: Pearson correlation between aligned source and target post-IBD edge responses
pairwise_transfer_surface.per_target_statistic: Pearson correlation across sources between v0.2 residualized host-resource similarity and transfer congruence
pairwise_transfer_surface.panel_statistic: arithmetic mean of finite target correlations

inference.p_value: maximum of +1 corrected one-sided upper-tail Monte Carlo p-values across all three nuisance references

stopping_rules: The v0.1 formal namespace is spent and cannot be reused for v0.2 qualification.
No v0.2 estimator component may change after any v0.2 formal statistic is inspected.
If any v0.2 gate fails, retire v0.2 and keep nucleotide identity closed.
No empirical genetic outcome from the new host-resource panel may be opened before all four gates pass.
